newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to pay Gazprom $239 mln in 1997 for debt.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to pay Gazprom $239 mln in 1997 for debt.

text.p: Ukraine's Finance Minister Valentyn Koronevsky on Thursday promised to honour a deal struck with Moscow restructuring a gas deal which foresees Russia's RAO Gazprom getting $239 million in 1997.
"Ukraine wants to pay $1.4 billion in foreign debts next year," Koronevsky told a news conference.
This would include $1.1 billion to countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States -- with $239 million going to Gazprom and $194 million to Turkmenistan for its gas supplies, he said.
Russia and Ukraine agreed at the end of 1994 to restructure Kiev's gas debt, with payments to be made over 12 years with two years' grace.
According to official Ukrainian figures, Ukraine owed Gazprom $1.477 billion at the end of 1994 and that had increased by $182.7 million a year later.

Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Pynzenyk told the news conference that restructuring of gas distribution in Ukraine and an increase in payments by consumers meant Kiev was not in debt to Russia or Turkmenistan for gas delivered this year.
The conference followed a meeting between President Leonid Kuchma and Gazprom chief Rem Vyakhirev on Wednesday where they agreed a bilateral gas deal should be drawn up for at least 20 years.

"This will remove the problem of the constant uncertainty about prices and conditions of gas supplies for Ukrainian producers," Kuchma's press service said, without giving exact details of how this would be achieved.
Kuchma told Vyakhirev Ukraine would move "very soon" from a monopolised system of gas supplies on the internal market to one based on market principles, the press service said.
Ukraine plans to import about 70 billion cubic metres of gas this year, with about 50 billion cubic metres coming from Russia and 20 billion from Turkmenistan.
This compares to Ukrainian planned gas output of 18.2 billion cubic metres.
